findings.description:
The skill tells the session "poll scrat status until it reports one of the four states below" and then "There are four, and each of them is below", but `runstate` has five states a run can rest in: `terminalStates = []State{Clean, Escalated, Failed, Cancelled}` (internal/runstate/state.go:19) plus the parked `awaiting-response`. `cancelled` is missing from the skill entirely.

Concrete path: the skill itself suggests the person run `scrat watch` in another terminal (messages.go:29), and README.md:57 documents `scrat watch` stopping "when you cancel it from another terminal". So: session starts a review, person watches, person runs `scrat cancel <run>`. `scrat status` now prints `state: cancelled` forever. The session's loop condition is "one of the four states below" and `cancelled` is not one of them, so the session polls indefinitely, or improvises with no instruction. `scrat respond` and `scrat continue` both refuse on a cancelled run, so there is nothing it can do either.

`TestEveryTerminalStateIsCovered` (internal/skill/skill_test.go:85) hardcodes the same four states, so nothing in the suite notices the omission. README.md:70 repeats the "four states" claim.

The check that backs the invariant "the skill names nothing the binary does not offer" has a live hole, because `surfaceOf` builds each command's flag set with `flagsIn` (internal/e2e/readers_test.go:76-80), which collects *every* `--`-prefixed token on every line of the `Flags:` block - including flag names that appear inside another flag's usage text.

Concrete case that exists today: `rejectedUsage = "the finding is wrong, and --reason says why"` (cmd/scrat/messages.go:23). So `scrat respond --help` renders `--reason` twice - once as its own flag line, once inside `--rejected`'s description - and `flagsIn` reports `--reason` as offered by `respond` on the strength of the description alone. Delete the `command.Flags().StringVar(&reason, "reason", ...)` line from cmd/scrat/respond.go:89 and `skill.Unavailable` still returns nothing, while the skill goes on instructing sessions to run `scrat respond --finding f2 --rejected --reason "..."` - which is precisely the "plausible and wrong at the point where the person has stopped watching" failure the requirement exists to prevent.

`TestARemovedFlagFailsTheSuite` does not cover this: it picks the first flag-bearing invocation `skill.Named()` returns, which is `{respond, --fixed}`, and `--fixed` appears in no other flag's description, so the guard passes and the hole stays.

Fix: in `flagsIn`, take only the first `--`-prefixed token per line (cobra puts the flag name first on each flag line).

The spec scenario this test is named for requires that `scrat watch` "appears in no loop the session is told to run" (openspec/changes/the-loop-an-agent-can-drive/specs/agent-skill/spec.md:57), and the skill puts it on the fourth line of numbered step 3 of "## The loop" (internal/skill/messages.go:29) - literally inside the session's own loop, as a suggestion.

The guard meant to catch that cannot: lines 61-65 already error unless `suggestion` contains "person", so `strings.Contains(numberedStep(...), "scrat watch") && !strings.Contains(suggestion, "person")` can never report a failure that line 63 has not already reported. The "appears in no loop" half of the scenario is therefore unverified.

Whether "a suggestion inside step 3" satisfies the spec is the author's call, but as it stands the spec text and the skill text disagree and no test distinguishes them.

`sectionAbout` bounds a section by cutting at `"
### "` only, so it does not stop at a level-2 heading. `awaiting-response` is the last `###` section in the document, so `sectionAbout(document, "awaiting-response")` returns its body *plus* the whole `## What socrates will not do for you` section (internal/skill/messages.go:61-71).

Consequence: `TestTheLoopCloses` (skill_test.go:139) and the `awaiting-response` case of `TestEveryTerminalStateIsCovered` assert over a region twice the size of the section they name. The prohibitions text mentions `scrat review`, and moving `scrat continue` or `scrat status` out of the parked-run instructions and into the prohibitions would leave `TestTheLoopCloses` green while the loop no longer closes. Cut at `"
## "` as well as `"
### "`.

`UserDirectory` puts the default install target at `~/.claude/skills`, which is exactly the tree the reviewer subprocess loads: the agent is invoked with `--setting-sources user` (internal/agent/claude.go:216, `settingSources = "user"`), which README.md:131 describes as the deliberate choice to keep the reviewed project's own agent instructions away from the reviewer.

So after `scrat skill`, every subsequent review spawns a reviewer whose available-skills list contains an entry named `scrat` described as "Have an independent reviewer read the change you just made, and drive that review to a verdict. Use after implementing anything nobody else has read", and the reviewer's `Read` tool can open the file. The blast radius is bounded - the reviewer's tools are `Read,Grep,Glob` (claude.go:21) so it cannot run scrat, and `OuterRun()` refuses a review inside a review - so this is context contamination rather than a defect. Naming it because the change writes into the one directory socrates is otherwise careful about.

The `escalated` section explains escalation with one cause only: "A finding that questions what the change is for is not one to patch your way out of, which is why the reviewer escalated it". A run also escalates when the two-round cap is reached with blocking findings still open (openspec/specs/review-dialogue/spec.md:86-89), and in that case the findings are patchable rather than questions of intent.

A session in that case is told to hand them over with the wrong explanation. Note that `scrat findings` will not correct it: `Findings.Lines()` prints `f.Reason` only when `!f.Reviewed` (internal/report/report.go:184-185), so the cap-reached reason never appears in the command the escalated section tells the session to read. It does appear in `scrat status`, which the session polled, so it is likely to have the reason in context - which is why this is informational rather than a defect.

`.serena/project.yml` (133 lines, almost all the upstream comment template) and `.serena/.gitignore` are committed by this change and have nothing to do with the stated intent or with the `the-loop-an-agent-can-drive` task list. Committing a project-level Serena config is a normal thing to do deliberately; flagging it only so the decision is a decision rather than a side effect of the branch.

This loop fails the suite for any word in the skill that contains `/` or ends in `.md`/`.txt`/`.json`/`.yaml`/`.yml`/`.log`. It passes today only because the current text happens to contain no path and no filename, and it does not actually establish the spec claim it is under ("names no command, flag or file through which a session could send the reviewer its own account") - a filename is neither necessary nor sufficient for that.

What it will do is fail on innocuous future edits: mentioning `~/.claude/skills/scrat/SKILL.md`, linking `AGENTS.md`, or writing "and/or" all trip it, with an error message that misdescribes the problem. The flag check above it (lines 42-49) is the part that carries the requirement.

risk_rationale: The production code added is small, side-effect-light and correct on the paths I traced; the risk sits in the deliverable itself - the skill omits the `cancelled` state and so teaches a loop with no exit for it - and in one verification check whose flag extraction can silently pass while the skill names a flag the binary no longer offers.
